PACE helps kids build connections through summer camps and trips
The Peabody Ambassadors Coalition for Education (PACE) is a program that allows students from Peabody to connect with and mentor students from Paul Cuffee Upper School in the Acushnet neighborhood of New Bedford.
PACE is designed to provide opportunities for students to bond and form friendships despite their differences. By taking part in summer camps and trips, the students have a chance to build connections and learn from one another.
There are two PACE programs: PACE North and PACE South. PACE North focuses on educational and personal development activities, while PACE South emphasizes community service and cultural experiences.
“Since its inception, PACE has been about building relationships, fostering a sense of community, and bridging the educational gap between our two schools,” said Elizabeth Wolf, a Peabody parent and PACE co-organizer.
During the 2018 summer, PACE North offered a 10-week program that included STEM camps, robotics, and a traditional summer camp experience. The students attended Cape Cod Academy and had the chance to participate in a variety of activities, including kayaking, hiking, and arts and crafts.
For PACE South, the program focused on community service and cultural experiences. The students attended the New Bedford Public Library and participated in various activities, such as the P.A.C.E. kids’ summer camp, which included a ropes course, arts and crafts, and other outdoor activities.
The program also included a summer trip to the Oak Bluffs community on Martha’s Vineyard, where the students learned about the island’s rich African American history and the history of the Martha’s Vineyard Playhouse.
PACE also provides PACE Parent Buddies, who help facilitate communication and fundraising efforts between the families of both schools. One of the goals of the program is to raise funds to support the programs and activities that benefit both schools.
“PACE Parent Buddies have been instrumental in helping to amplify the impact of PACE on our students and our community,” Wolf said. “By having a clear understanding of the needs of our students and the benefits of this program, they have enabled us to be more strategic and intentional in our fundraising efforts, leading to even more opportunities for our students.”
At the core of PACE is the recognition that social connections are essential for the well-being and success of students. The program provides a framework for building relationships and developing meaningful friendships, which in turn, can enhance students’ educational experiences and support their personal growth.

^{a} School of Chemical and Biomedical Engineering, Cork Institute of Technology, Bishopstown, Cork, Ireland
^{b} Instituto de Investigación en Ingeniería de Procesos (IIIP), Departamento de Ingeniería Química, Universidad de Santiago de Chile, Avenida Ecuador 2849, Santiago, Chile
This study explores the use of hybrid zeolite materials in the delignification and anthocyanin extraction from grape waste. Delignification was carried out using NaOH (5%, w/v) as a control and in the presence of two hybrid zeolites, ZSM-5-β (SiO 2 /Al 2 O 3 /Na 2 O/K 2 O) and β-zeolite-imidazolate (SiO 2 /Al 2 O 3 /NIT) and two zeolites: β-zeolite and ZSM-5. After 90 min of treatment at 90 °C, the β-zeolite-imidazolate showed a more significant lignin removal (43.6%) compared to β-zeolite (39.8%) and ZSM-5 (34.2%). The hybrid zeolite materials with imidazolate framework have shown an increased extractability of anthocyanins in comparison to the beta and ZSM-5 zeolites alone. Anthocyanin extractability (on dry basis) was 12.1% for β-zeolite-imidazolate, 10.3% for β-zeolite and 9.4% for ZSM-5, compared to 7.1% for the control. Additionally, mass spectrometry imaging analysis suggested that in the presence of hybrid zeolite β-zeolite-imidazolate the crude extract contained more intact polyphenols. The delignification efficiency of hybrid zeolites was a function of their structure, Si/Al ratio, and the presence of imidazolate framework. These results indicate the hybrid zeolites have potential for selective and efficient delignification and anthocyanin extraction from grape waste. The results of this study show that the hybrid zeolites are more effective compared to commercial zeolites for the desired application. These hybrid materials have potential for scaling up the production of valuable compounds from agro-food waste materials

EQUALS Global Partnership – Challenging inequality through technology
The EQUALS Global Partnership aims to address the technology-related inequalities that affect girls and women around the world, aiming to achieve SDG 5 – Gender Equality by 2030.
While women make up nearly half of the world’s population, they make up only a quarter of tech professionals, with the numbers falling to just 11% in some countries. Digital technologies are transformative tools, but for women and girls, full access and benefits are still a dream for millions, waiting to be fulfilled.
There are many reasons why fewer women than men become tech professionals and entrepreneurs, including stereotypes, bias, lack of access to education and opportunity, lack of representation in business and policy, and many other barriers. This is not just an issue for women and girls, but for societies that miss out on their talents, innovations, and economic contributions.
However, women and girls already have a significant presence in tech, and it’s not too late to change the game. Grassroots and community-led initiatives, research and public education campaigns, and partnership among policymakers, private sector companies, and non-profit organizations can make a significant impact.
So, what are the key outcomes of EQUALS Global Partnership?
Connecting girls and women with opportunities for education, skills training, employment, and entrepreneurship in the tech sector;
Challenging stereotypes and bias through education, advocacy, and media campaigns;
Increasing the number of girls and women in tech professions and decision-making positions;
Promoting technology use to improve women’s health, economic empowerment, and safety;
Empowering women to be leaders and agents of change in the technology ecosystem.

Join the conversation on social media using the hashtag #EQUALS, and share your ideas and experiences.

Participate in regional and global forums and discussions that shape the future of technology and development.

Novel Triterpenoid Analog
I n this paper, we will cover a novel triterpenoid analog that has demonstrated significant potential in medical research, particularly in its applications as an anti-inflammatory agent. The triterpenoid analog (TA) is a structural variation of the well-studied compound, which naturally occurs in various plants, including agallocha, helianthus annuus, and others.
The novel TA has been synthesized through a series of chemical reactions that have altered the molecular structure from the original triterpenoid. This alteration aims to enhance its biological activity, particularly in reducing inflammation. Research has focused on identifying and isolating compounds with potential anti-inflammatory effects from plant extracts. By synthesizing a novel analog, researchers can precisely control the structure and modify its properties to optimize its effectiveness.
Anti-inflammatory Activity
Inflammation is a complex physiological response to tissue damage or infection, characterized by increased blood flow, white blood cell invasion, and various chemical mediators. Chronic or excessive inflammation has been associated with various diseases, including arthritis, asthma, and certain cancers. Consequently, identifying effective anti-inflammatory agents has become an important goal in modern medicine.
Preliminary studies have demonstrated the novel TA has exhibited potent anti-inflammatory activity, comparable to established drugs like corticosteroids. This makes it a promising candidate for further clinical trials and potential use in treating chronic inflammatory conditions. Research also explores its effectiveness against specific disease states, such as rheumatoid arthritis and inflammatory bowel disease.
Mechanism of Action
While the exact mechanism by which the novel TA reduces inflammation is still under investigation, it is believed to act at several points in the inflammatory cascade. One possibility is its interaction with enzymes involved in the formation of pro-inflammatory mediators, such as COX-2 and lipoxygenase. By inhibiting these enzymes, the TA may reduce the production of prostaglandins and leukotrienes, which contribute to inflammation.

Targeted Therapy
The novel TA has the potential to provide targeted therapy, avoiding the systemic side effects associated with broad-spectrum anti-inflammatory agents. Its specificity could result from its interaction with unique molecular targets or its localization within the inflamed tissue. This targeted approach might also minimize the risk of adverse effects and improve patient compliance, especially in long-term treatments.

Conclusion

William Herschel was a musical astronomer (he discovered the planet Uranus by accident!) who had an important thought experiment. He asked what would happen if a giant sound wave were traveling through space. He speculated that it might have an effect on other celestial objects, even planets.

Well, we can actually do a simulation of that very idea. We’ll consider a simplified model in which we allow a range of different frequencies of pressure waves to travel through space.

To make things simple, we will focus on two phenomena: (1) does the pressure wave have enough energy to disrupt nearby objects, like a planet? And (2) does the pressure wave have a significant effect on the flow of a surrounding fluid, such as space gas?

For these purposes, we consider the standard shockwave equation, which is used to solve the nonlinear wave equation, a simple nonlinear wave propagation equation.

We find that the shockwave has three very distinct regimes. In regime one (shock-free flow), the pressure wave’s Mach number is low, so the fluid’s speed is below the speed of sound. The shockwave has little effect on the flow. For regime two (shock presence), the Mach number exceeds 1, so the shock is able to compress the gas. Regime three is when the Mach number is very high, above some critical threshold (about 3.46). The Mach number itself stabilizes over time.

Using a more complex model, namely an equation of state that includes the thermal and vibration components, we include additional physics in our simulations.

We observe that the large pressure waves become trapped and get reflected off larger objects, such as gas giant planets.

We also simulate (and measure) the following key properties: the most energetic shock components, shock core speeds, radiation flux on exposed surfaces, the Richardson scale, and lift forces due to radiation.

We combine our study to derive various useful results. The first is an important expression for the Mach number threshold. The second finding is that hydrostatic updrafts can occur, characterized by the Richardson scale.

Rent increases up, downtown evictions down, new housing infrastructure
Potential increases in residential rent in Austin are once again a point of contention among council members and local housing advocates. On one hand, the median rent in the city has risen to $1,644, with an average increase of 7.1 percent in 2020.
On the other hand, “no-cause” evictions – or the ability to evict a tenant without a valid reason – are on the decline. According to data from the City of Austin’s housing and planning department, no-cause evictions decreased by 11 percent between 2019 and 2020. Those figures are somewhat of a silver lining to the rent increases.
Additionally, City Council recently identified and agreed to invest in various infrastructure projects aimed at increasing the supply of housing, including constructing new homes, apartments, and multifamily units in multiple locations. These projects are designed to support the city’s goal of adding 100,000 new housing units by 2025.
While these developments may present some optimism in the housing market, real affordability and affordability challenges persist in Austin, according to housing advocates. “We need to confront the root causes of unaffordability head-on, and that includes addressing speculation, short-term rentals, and predatory lending practices,” said Michael Wilson, a housing policy advocate with the Front Steps Homeless Prevention Center. “Building new units is just part of the solution.”
The most affected areas of town remain the ones with the smallest (and most expensive) average home prices, according to online real estate platform Zillow. Based on current data, some of the most “unaffordable” neighborhoods for first-time buyers include:
Eastside’s Govalle neighborhood (#1) – average home value: $430,000;
Clarksville neighborhood (#2) – average home value: $429,000;
South Congress (#3) – average home value: $415,000.
More homeowners in these areas can sell their homes to developers or more affluent buyers, thereby contributing to rising prices and continued housing unaffordability in those neighborhoods, advocates say. So, why might home prices rise in these areas and continue to create affordability issues?
Residents argue that property investors and developers benefit greatly from government investments and interest in revitalizing once-forgotten neighborhoods. To further accelerate the gentrification of Austin, some property owners are installing lots of small short-term rentals, often sacrificing units for apartment or single-family homes in the interests of the vacation rental market.

Outcome of patients with sleep apnea receiving nasal CPAP (CPAP) therapy: A multicenter study
This study looks at the effects of continuous positive airway pressure (CPAP) therapy on patients with sleep apnea. CPAP therapy involves the use of a mask to deliver a constant stream of air pressure into the patient's airways during sleep, helping to prevent the airway from collapsing and causing breathing pauses.
The study enrolled 384 patients who had been diagnosed with sleep apnea, half of whom were men and half of whom were women. The patients were treated with CPAP therapy for 6-8 hours per night and were monitored over a period of 6-12 months to assess their response to treatment.
The results of the study show that, after 6-12 months of CPAP therapy, the patients experienced significant improvements in their sleep apnea symptoms, including:
* A reduction in the number of episodes of sleep apnea per hour of sleep (apnea-hypopnea index)
* Improved oxygen saturation levels
* Reduced symptoms of daytime sleepiness
* Improved overall quality of life
These results are consistent with the known benefits of CPAP therapy for patients with sleep apnea, which include improved respiratory health, reduced risk of cardiovascular disease, and improved overall quality of life.
The study's findings are consistent with those of previous studies, which have also shown that CPAP therapy can lead to significant improvements in sleep apnea symptoms and quality of life. The study's results are likely to be of interest to healthcare providers who treat patients with sleep apnea and to patients who are considering CPAP therapy as a treatment option. GREEK DISHES YOU HAVE TO TRY!
Welcome to Greek cuisine!
With its rich history and geography, Greece has a rich culinary tradition that's deeply rooted in Mediterranean flavors and ingredients. From hearty meat stews to crispy vegetables, creamy dips and refreshing salads, Greek cuisine is all about the simple pleasures of life. Here are some of the most iconic Greek dishes you have to try!
Gyro (Γύρος)
Thinly sliced meat (usually pork, chicken, or beef) stacked on a vertical spit and served in a warm pita with tomato, onion, cucumber, and tzatziki sauce (a refreshing yogurt-based condiment).
Moussaka (Μουσακά)
Layered eggplant, ground meat, and a creamy bechamel sauce, making for a hearty, satisfying main course.
Souvlaki (Σουβλάκι)
Juicy skewers of marinated meat (usually pork or chicken) grilled to perfection and served with a side of tangy tzatziki sauce.
Greek Salad (Ελληνικό SALAD)
A simple yet delicious salad featuring juicy tomatoes, crumbled feta cheese, red onion, and Kalamata olives, dressed with olive oil and a squeeze of lemon juice.
Dolmades (Δολμάδες)
Stuffed grape leaves filled with a mix of rice, ground meat, and spices, often served as an appetizer or side dish.
Spanakopita (Σπανακόπιτα)
A spinach and feta cheese pie wrapped in flaky phyllo pastry, perfect as a snack or light meal.
Stifado (Στιφάδο)
A rich, flavorful beef stew cooked in a sweet and spicy sauce, often served with mashed potatoes or rice.
Tiropita (Τυρόπιτα)
A cheese pie made with crumbled feta and phyllo pastry, perfect as a snack or side dish.
Loukoumades (Λουκουμάδες)
Deep-fried dough balls drizzled with honey and sprinkled with cinnamon, a sweet treat you'll love!

Earlier this week, H-Project (Heavy Industries) announced a crowdfunding campaign on Patreon to support the development of its open-source engine, Simahoo, formerly code-named Heavy Industries Sunny.
The funding campaign has already exceeded its initial $20,000 target, with contributors offering financial support in exchange for exclusive content, early access to new features, and other perks.
H-Project is a Serbian-based gaming company that has gained a following for its work on the Soviet-era theme, with titles such as Gulag Manager and the engine’s predecessor, Simahoo (formerly known as Heavy Industries Sunny).
The open-source engine, which has been in development for five years, aims to provide a free and customizable game engine that can be used to develop a wide range of games. Simahoo promises support for various platforms, including PC, consoles, and web-based platforms.
The engine’s core features include a flexible graphics engine, advanced physics, and a dynamic sound system. Simahoo also supports multi-threading, dynamic lighting, and shadows.
In addition to the core engine, H-Project plans to release various tools and plugins that will make it easier for developers to create content using Simahoo.
By leveraging the power of open-source development, Simahoo offers a free alternative to commercial game engines like Unity and Unreal Engine. This could make it more accessible to indie developers and developers with limited budgets.
The crowdfunding campaign for Simahoo will continue until January 31st, 2024, and supporters can contribute from $5 to $1,000 or more, depending on their level of support. All contributors will receive exclusive rewards, including access to exclusive content, beta versions of the engine, and early access to new features.
In a separate statement, H-Project mentioned that a percentage of the crowdfunding proceeds will go towards supporting development of new features, hiring more team members, and other operational expenses. The remaining funds will be used to further invest in the engine and implement feature requests.
More details on the funding campaign and rewards offered can be found on the Patreon page. Contributors can also join the Simahoo community to stay up-to-date on the engine’s development, learn from the community, and participate in the engine’s design and feature planning.

Peacefully, with family by her side, Mary Lulu Linag Isle, aged 92, passed away on July 7, 2011. She is predeceased by her loving husband of 65 years, Peter. She is remembered by her children, Ronald and Sylvia; their spouses, Masa and Mogens; and her five grandchildren, Derek, Allison, Michelle, Rebecca, and Torsten. Mary is also remembered by her great-grandchildren, Maya, Leonardo, Emil, Oliver, Hazel, Livia, and Isaak. Born in Bissett, Ontario on October 15, 1918, she was the only child of Malcolm and Bessie Linag. Her family soon moved to Scotland and then to Virginia, USA. During World War II, she worked as an air warden in Winnipeg, Manitoba. After the war, she moved to Canada, met her husband in Pusan, Korea, and married in Toronto in 1946. They soon moved to Vancouver, where Mary was active in the Bethel Lutheran Church and the Canadian Women's Auxiliary Airforce. Mary will be remembered for her kind, gentle, and generous spirit, her love of travel, her devotion to her family, and her long-standing commitment to social justice. The family would like to express their gratitude to the staff at L'Arche Vancouver for their care and compassion during her later years. Funeral services will be held on Monday, July 11, at 11:00 am at St. Mark's Lutheran Church. Interment to follow. In lieu of flowers, donations to the L'Arche Vancouver Fund or the Bethel Lutheran Church would be appreciated. Rest in peace, dear Lulu. Mosquito-borne diseases in the Nigerian context
Mosquitoes are responsible for spreading some of the deadliest diseases known to humans. In the Nigerian context, mosquitoes are responsible for transmitting diseases such as malaria, yellow fever, and filariasis. These diseases are prevalent in Nigeria and have a significant impact on the country’s health and economy. In this article, we will discuss the mosquito-borne diseases prevalent in Nigeria, their causes, symptoms, diagnosis, treatment, and prevention.
Malaria is a mosquito-borne disease caused by Plasmodium parasites transmitted by the bite of an infected female Anopheles mosquito. It is a major public health problem in Nigeria, with an estimated 10-20% of the population infected. Symptoms of malaria include fever, chills, flu-like symptoms, and anemia. Diagnosis is usually made by microscopy or rapid diagnostic test, and treatment involves the use of antimalarial drugs.
Yellow fever is another mosquito-borne disease prevalent in Nigeria, caused by a flavivirus transmitted by the bite of an infected Aedes mosquito. Symptoms of yellow fever include fever, headache, fatigue, and liver failure. Diagnosis is made by serological tests, and treatment involves supportive care. Yellow fever vaccine is available and is recommended for all travelers to areas where the disease is prevalent.
Filariasis, also known as elephantiasis, is a mosquito-borne disease caused by filarial parasites transmitted by the bite of an infected Culex mosquito. Symptoms of filariasis include swelling of the limbs, pain, and skin discoloration. Diagnosis is made by microscopy, and treatment involves the use of antifilarial drugs.
Prevention of mosquito-borne diseases in Nigeria involves several strategies, including:
1. Use of insecticide-treated bed nets (ITNs) and indoor residual spraying (IRS)
2. Elimination of breeding sites
3. Use of repellents and protective clothing
4. Early detection and treatment of disease cases
5. Immunization against yellow fever
6. Vector control measures, such as larval control and adult mosquito control
In conclusion, mosquito-borne diseases are a significant public health problem in Nigeria, with malaria, yellow fever, and filariasis being the major diseases. Prevention and control of these diseases require a multi-faceted approach that involves government, healthcare workers, and the community. It is essential to educate the public on the causes, symptoms, diagnosis, treatment, and prevention of these diseases to reduce their impact on the country’s health and economy.

Immutable Bit Rot Transform (IBRT)
The Immutable Bit Rot Transform (IBRT) is a symmetric cipher proposed in 2015. IBRT uses two permutation matrices S _{8,0} and S _{8,1} and a bitwise rotation matrix R _{8,6} to perform a bit rotation in parallel over eight-bit blocks. IBRT is resistant against side channel attacks like timing attacks and timing power analysis (TPA) because of its simple and constant time operations.
IBRT is not more secure than AES. Yet it has been a part of the National Cipher Challenge, which is a math and programming contest run by the British Society for the History of Mathematics.
IBRT has been implemented in Haskell in Cryptanium, a set of cryptographic algorithms in Haskell. This is a set of cryptographic algorithms in Haskell, written to be concise, readable, and verified with QuickCheck. IBRT has been analyzed in the study of "Correctness, Security, and Performance of IBRT and LSS" (2017) and in the study of "Computational Power and Potential Applications of IBRT" (2018).

A. no
B. C
C. D
D. yes
Answer: D
Explanation: Krueppel-like factor 4 (KLF4) plays an important role in various cellular processes, including cell growth, differentiation, and apoptosis. However, the role of KLF4 in trophoblast invasion and proliferation, as well as the underlying signaling pathways involved, remains poorly understood. In this study, we aimed to investigate the expression and function of KLF4 in trophoblast cells and determine its involvement in the regulation of trophoblast invasion and proliferation through the PI3K/AKT signaling pathway.
Trophoblast cells HTR-8/SVneo were cultured and treated with different reagents. The expression of KLF4, PI3K, AKT, p-AKT, E-cadherin, N-cadherin, VEGFA, and MMP-2 was detected by RT-PCR, Western blot, or immunofluorescence staining. The activity of PI3K and AKT was determined by enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay (ELISA). The motility and invasion of trophoblast cells were measured by wound healing and transwell assay.
KLF4 expression was significantly upregulated in HTR-8/SVneo cells in response to EGF treatment. The PI3K/AKT signaling pathway was activated in HTR-8/SVneo cells after EGF treatment. Notably, KLF4 knockdown suppressed EGF-induced PI3K/AKT activation, and decreased the expression of VEGFA and MMP-2, while enhancing E-cadherin expression and reducing cell motility and invasion. Moreover, PI3K/AKT activation was inhibited by the PI3K inhibitor LY294002, which also significantly suppressed KLF4 expression, VEGFA and MMP-2 expression, and trophoblast cell invasion and proliferation.
Our results suggest that KLF4 is involved in the regulation of trophoblast invasion and proliferation through the PI3K/AKT signaling pathway, and that EGF may regulate these processes by activating KLF4 and the PI3K/AKT signaling pathway. Paul talks about grace (or undeserved blessings) being effective and remaining effective, as we turn towards Christ who effects our personal relationships and reconcile us to one another, including those outside the family of God. Just as we put the old “man” behind us, we must stop attributing grace to it, and view the new “man” in Christ, filled with the Holy Spirit, as the source of our proper and acceptable relationships. The circle of blessing involves acceptance by Christ, recognition of all the faithful “fruits” already there, and growing in appreciation of Christ and our new relationships as we reconcile with God and with one another.

Those who precede us left moral certainties behind to believe in Christ, as Paul awaits to be with God’s people who have a consistent relationship with him and is waiting for a day when the universe fully reveals Christ, that includes redemption through his blood, and knowledge of the mystery of God.

Impact of soil erosion on Wheat productivity in northern Ghana
Ghana is a country with rich arable land, natural vegetation cover, and renewable water resources. However, the country is experiencing increasing soil erosion resulting from deforestation, over-grazing, poor agricultural practices, and a prolonged dry spell that often leads to low crop yields, poverty and food insecurity. This paper examined the impact of soil erosion on wheat productivity in northern Ghana. A survey was conducted in northern Ghana covering 250 wheat farmers. Secondary data were collected from the agricultural extension officer in Northern Region. Field observations were conducted in three districts of Northern Region. Wheat yield and farmers' perceptions of soil erosion were significant and related variables. Factors that influenced wheat yield included the use of conservation tillage, agroforestry and application of manure. A positive correlation existed between use of conservation tillage, agroforestry and application of manure and wheat productivity. Wheat productivity and erosion depth were negatively correlated. Farmers perceived soil erosion as a significant factor that affects wheat productivity. The study recommended conservation of soil, use of conservation tillage and agroforestry and application of manure to reduce soil erosion and increase wheat productivity. Farmers should be trained on how to manage soil erosion through conservation of soil and planting cover crops to reduce land degradation and restore soil fertility for sustainable wheat productivity.

Honoring Mary Fishburn and Becoming Part of the Qs Story
In 2010, the Pro Football Hall of Fame Museum in Canton, Ohio was undergoing an expansion project that included the construction of a multi-media, interactive exhibit space, called the Radio Days Gallery, honoring the memories of Radio Voices of the Game. Of particular importance was the role radio play-by-play announcers had in sustaining the game of football during the Great Depression and World War II years, when traveling to games was not feasible for fans, radio was the only way to hear the game.
During the project, it became apparent that the Mary Fishburn oral history files at the Center for Archival Collections (CAC) were essential in researching the history of the Cleveland Browns and NFL radio broadcasts in the region. Researchers used my 2002 interviews to clarify specific historical events and facts. This collaboration allowed for the creation of an exhibit that truly reflected the impact of radio play-by-play announcers on the fans of Cleveland and the game as a whole.
One of the stories in the exhibit was about Ray Lange, who played for the Cleveland Browns and later became a radio play-by-play announcer, broadcasting for the Browns for a number of years. After checking the oral history files at the CAC, we confirmed what Lange had told me during our 2002 interview, that he had played for the Browns during the early days of the team and had later broadcast the team. Another story in the exhibit was about Martin Harris, who broadcast Cleveland Browns games for over 20 years. I had interviewed him in 2001, and researchers at the Hall of Fame contacted the CAC to access his oral history files to gather more information about his broadcasting career with the Browns.
The connections that were made with the Pro Football Hall of Fame staff during the exhibit development were truly rewarding. The exhibit was well-received, and the Hall of Fame decided to dedicate an entire day to celebrating the impact of radio voices on the game of football in the region. They invited my friend, retired Browns radio play-by-play announcer, Ray Lane, and me to be the guest speakers for this event. It was an honor to be a part of this celebration, and we received a wonderful reception from the attendees.

Junwen Qian: Composition analysis of high-dimensional data using dictionary learning
High-dimensional data is common in various fields, such as bioinformatics and computer vision. Dictionary learning is a popular method for representing high-dimensional data in a lower-dimensional space, which leads to better interpretation and analysis of the data. However, the performance of dictionary learning algorithms largely depends on the choice of the dictionary, and it is challenging to obtain a good dictionary from data with strong correlations or structures.
In this talk, I will introduce our recent work on learning a structured dictionary for high-dimensional data analysis. Our method is based on a novel formulation of dictionary learning, which incorporates prior knowledge of the data structures. This approach can effectively capture complex patterns in the data, and leads to improved performance of data analysis tasks, such as feature extraction and anomaly detection. Experimental results on several real-world datasets demonstrate the effectiveness of our method in comparison with state-of-the-art methods.
Bio: Junwen Qian received her Ph.D. in Electrical and Computer Engineering from the University of Illinois at Urbana-Champaign in 2019. Her research interests include machine learning, signal processing, and computational statistics, with a focus on big data and high-dimensional data analysis. She has published several papers in top-tier conferences and journals in her field, including NIPS, ICLR, and IEEE T-SP. She is currently a postdoctoral researcher at the University of Illinois at Urbana-Champaign. Her research has been supported by several awards, including the NBER/NSF Fellowship and the Best Student Paper Award at the IEEE Workshop on Machine Learning for Signal Processing.

Wrongful death claims can be complex and emotionally challenging to navigate. Losing a loved one can be traumatic, and knowing how to approach a wrongful death claim can seem overwhelming. The right guidance can help you better understand your rights and the steps you need to take.

### What Is a Wrongful Death Claim?

A wrongful death claim is a lawsuit filed by the surviving family members or estate of a person who died due to the negligence, reckless behavior, or intentional act of another individual or entity. These claims can be brought against a wide range of defendants, including businesses, healthcare providers, government entities, and private individuals.

To file a wrongful death claim, you typically need to prove the following:

1.  **Duty of Care**: The defendant owed the decedent a duty of care, which was breached in some way.
2.  **Causation**: The breach of duty caused the decedent's death.
3.  **Damages**: The decedent's surviving family members or estate have suffered damages as a result of the decedent's death.

### What Are the Types of Damages Recoverable in a Wrongful Death Claim?

In a wrongful death claim, you can recover various types of damages, including:

1.  **Compensatory Damages**: These damages are designed to compensate the family for their financial losses, including lost income, funeral expenses, medical bills, and other related costs.
2.  **Punitive Damages**: These damages are intended to punish the defendant for their reckless or intentional behavior and to deter similar behavior in the future.
3.  **Emotional Damages**: These damages compensate the family for their emotional pain and suffering, including grief, depression, anxiety, and other related psychological injuries.

### How Do You File a Wrongful Death Claim?

To file a wrongful death claim, you typically need to:

1.  **Gather Evidence**: Collect and preserve all relevant evidence, including medical records, police reports, witness statements, and other documentation.

Unity is one of the most popular game engines for developing VR applications, and SteamVR has a dedicated plugin for Unity that makes it easy to integrate SteamVR features into your Unity project.
Here's how to install the SteamVR Plugin for Unity:
**Step 1: Download and Install the SteamVR Plugin**
1. Go to the [SteamVR Plugin for Unity GitHub page](https://github.com/ValveSoftware/steamvr_for_unity) and click on the **Clone or download** button.
2. Select **Download ZIP** and save the file to your computer.
3. Extract the contents of the zip file to a folder on your computer.
4. Open your Unity project and go to **Window** > **Package Manager**.
5. Click on the **+** button at the top left corner of the Package Manager window and select **Add package from disk**.
6. Navigate to the folder where you extracted the SteamVR Plugin and select the **steamvr_for_unity.unitypackage** file.

**Step 2: Import the SteamVR Plugin**
1. Click on **Import** to import the SteamVR Plugin into your Unity project.
2. Once the import is complete, you should see a new **SteamVR** menu item in the **Window** menu.
3. Close the Package Manager window.

**Step 3: Configure the SteamVR Plugin**
1. Go to **Window** > **SteamVR** > **SteamVR Plugin**.
2. In the SteamVR Plugin window, make sure that the **Enabled** checkbox is selected.
3. Click on the **Update Plugin** button to update the plugin to the latest version.

That's it! You have now successfully installed the SteamVR Plugin for Unity. You can now start using SteamVR features such as VR rendering, input, and tracking in your Unity project.

If you encounter any issues during the installation process, here are some common solutions:

* If you're using a 64-bit operating system, make sure that you're using the 64-bit version of the SteamVR Plugin.
* If you're having trouble installing the plugin, try restarting Unity and trying again.

This technical paper reports on our experimental studies of vapor-liquid separation in a _sudden expansion_--a field that heretofore has received little attention. It is our belief that this problem has been largely overlooked in the past and that the results obtained in this field should be of value to chemists and chemical engineers.
**Theory and Apparatus**
The _sudden expansion_ is a rapid expansion of two-phase mixture in which the physical properties change continuously in a way different from expansion in which a liquid is expanded with nucleation. Basic consideration of this problem is based on a quasi-equilibrium assumption, according to which the state of vapor and liquid before and after the expansion are considered to be in equilibrium with one another. However, whether this assumption is justified or not is still a matter for debate. In fact, because a sudden expansion is concerned with the relationship between the rate of mass transfer and the local physical properties and flows, it is a highly non-equilibrium process and the quasi-equilibrium assumption is likely to be poor.
The sudden expansion used in this study consisted of a vertical _V_-\(\times\) 1/4-in. tube of 30-in. length. The mixture flowed through the horizontal tube into the vertical section, and the vapor and liquid separated at the very top of the vertical tube, and the velocities of these two phases were measured at a predetermined point below this point of separation. All experimental runs were made in steady state, and pressures were measured at the very top of the vertical tube. All velocity measurements were taken at a point 1 in. from the point of expansion.

1.真菌的生命周期:
真菌的生命周期通常包括以下几个阶段：孢子、菌丝、菌Spot和孢子囊。不同的真菌种类可能会有不同的生命周期，但这些阶段是普遍的。
 
-孢子：真菌孢子是真菌生命周期的第一阶段。孢子是坚硬、无菌丝的微小结构，可以作为真菌传播的媒介。
-菌丝：在孢子落地后，菌丝开始生长和分化。如果孢子在适当的生长条件下落地，它会吸收周围的营养物质并进行繁殖，从而形成菌丝。
-菌Spot：菌丝会继续生长并形成菌孢子囊。在一些真菌中，菌孢子囊内会形成许多孢子。这也称为孢子中心。
-孢子囊：孢子囊包含孢子，孢子囊的制毒能力对于某些真菌生存至关重要。

2.真菌与生态环境的相互作用:
真菌扮演了生态环境中的重要角色，它们可以作为食物链的底物，提供营养物质，并起着对环境的重要调节作用。
-真菌作为食物链的底物:真菌可以作为种子植物和其他生物的腐植体来源，这为当地的食物链和物种多样性提供了种子。
-真菌的营养作用:一些真菌分解有机物，释放营养物质，使其在土壤中更容易被其他生物利用，从而促进土壤有机物的循环。
-真菌调节环境中的营养物质:真菌还可以分解长期停留在土壤中的氮和磷，释放这些营养物质，使其再次被用作植物的营养来源。

Transient development of mitogen-activated protein kinases in response to atrial stretch.
Abstract/OtherAbstract: BACKGROUND: Mitogen-activated protein kinases (MAPKs) have been implicated in the pathophysiology of cardiac hypertrophy. We hypothesized that atrial stretch could activate MAPKs in the heart. METHODS: Atrial stretch was induced by an inflated left atrial balloon in anesthetized dogs. MAPKs (ERK1/2, JNK, and p38) were assessed in the left atrium by Western blotting. RESULTS: Atrial stretch for 20 to 60 minutes induced significant activation of ERK1/2, JNK, and p38, with peak responses at 20 minutes. ERK1/2 was most prominently activated, and it returned to baseline by 120 minutes. JNK activation was observed for up to 180 minutes, whereas p38 activation persisted for 240 minutes. Phosphatidylinositol 3-kinase and Akt were also activated in response to atrial stretch, suggesting a role for these signaling molecules in mediating MAPK activation. In isolated rat atrial myocytes, thapsigargin-activated calcium influx induced MAPK activation similar to atrial stretch, suggesting a role for calcium in MAPK activation. CONCLUSION: Atrial stretch induces transient activation of MAPKs in the heart, with different MAPKs activated for distinct durations. This activation may be relevant to the adaptation of the atrium to increased stretch, a common phenomenon in heart failure.

NEW CHALLENGES FOR NATIONALISM
Alfred Stepan
Although much has changed, nationalism remains a central element in the lives of people and governments. The rise of new nationalisms and the rejuvenation of old ones are transforming the national landscape. This essay suggests that while nationalism may be experiencing new difficulties, there are many more than enough nationalisms, forms of it, and variations of it to redefine the nation-state in many creative ways.
This paper will examine four trends in the _supranationalism_, the emergence of new _transnational_ groups, the resurgence of _subnational_ nationalisms, and the presence of _ethno-nationalist_ mobilization in the shadow of democracy in some countries.
Both supranationalism, which enables greater sharing of power and resources, and transnationalism, which bridges national groups across borders, can help diminish the appeal of nationalism. New supranational arrangements, especially the European Union, are reshaping national relationships and institutional frameworks. The emergence of new transnational groups and alliances, including global civil society, allows people from different national groups to connect and interact as "global citizens" rather than as purely national citizens.

EUROPEAN INTEGRATION:
FROM COOPERATION TO FEDERATION?
Otto Borchert and Maria Zervakis
The integration of Europe is facing new challenges since the adoption of the Amsterdam Treaty. After presenting an overview of the post-Maastricht era developments, the paper argues that a shift towards a deeper level of political integration has become unavoidable in order to achieve an effective EU citizenship and a more flexible and dynamic EU employment market, both of which are required by the economic and social changes of the contemporary era.
The White Paper on European Governance and the Draft Constitution of the EU can be seen as first steps towards a more unified and directly democratic form of government. The European Convention represents a key moment in the transition from cooperation to a federal-like system of government. The Constitutional Convention has laid the foundation for a treaty on a European Constitution, which may culminate in a federal-like system of government. The process towards a federal system is not going to be easy, especially given the variety of institutional, economic, and social conditions in the 15 member states of the EU.

Overview and Objective
This module aims to develop students' critical thinking and analytical skills through the study of a number of key themes and issues in the history of art. By focusing on a series of case studies and featuring a range of approaches, techniques and art forms, the course will demonstrate the versatility and diversity of art historical methods and knowledge.
Students will have the opportunity to critically evaluate the stylistic, historical and cultural contexts of a selection of art historical movements and themes. By examining the ways in which art forms can be used to convey different meanings and to represent various ideas, students will learn to think critically about the production, reception and interpretation of art.
By the end of the module, students will be able to:
Analyse and interpret a range of artworks and art historical contexts
Critically evaluate the historiographical debates surrounding specific art movements and themes
Discuss the cultural and social factors that have influenced the production, reception and interpretation of art
Demonstrate an understanding of the role of art in shaping and reflecting cultural values
Course Contents:
Week 1: Introduction to Art History and Critical Thinking
Review of art historical methods and approaches
Overview of key debates and issues in art history
Week 2-3: Renaissance Art and Humanism
The cultural and artistic developments of the Renaissance
The humanist ideals and their representation in art
Week 4-5: The Baroque and the Experience of Time
The cultural and artistic developments of the Baroque period
The representation of time and the sublime in art
Week 6-7: Romanticism and the Rise of Modern Art
The cultural and artistic developments of Romanticism
The representation of nature and the sublime in art
Week 8-9: Modern Art Movements and the Challenge to Tradition
The cultural and artistic developments of Modernism
The representation of abstraction and the challenge to traditional representation
Week 10-11: Contemporary Art and the Question of Identity
The cultural and artistic developments of contemporary art
The representation of identity and the challenge to traditional notions of self
Week 12: Review and Assessment
Critical evaluation of the course and the development of critical thinking skills
Assessment:
There will be two written assignments (40% each) of 1,500 words each. The first assignment will be due on Week 9 and will explore the ways in which humanist ideals were represented in Renaissance art. The second assignment will be due on Week 12 and will evaluate the significance of modern art movements in challenging traditional notions of representation.

Audit Finds Millions Missing From DC Government
By Tom Sherwood
A city auditor's report to the D.C. Council finds millions of dollars are missing from the District of Columbia government's books.
The audit, obtained by WTOP, shows that the District missed about $44 million in tax payments in 2013, not counting $16 million from uncollected parking fines.
The report also found that agencies failed to properly report $29 million in various programs, leading to inaccurate financial statements.
The auditor also discovered that the District is underestimating its liabilities by millions. The District's Comprehensive Annual Financial Report lists $6.8 billion in outstanding debt, but the auditor found that's actually $745 million more than that.
"They need to not just improve their accounting practices, but their data collection practices, their reporting practices and basically, their entire fiscal management system," said D.C. Council Chairman Phil Mendelson (D-At-Large).
The audit report calls for the D.C. Office of the Chief Financial Officer (CFO) to take steps to improve financial management and internal controls.
"We will review the recommendations of the audit and work to ensure that we make the necessary improvements to prevent these types of issues from happening in the future," said a spokesperson for the CFO.
The council is holding a hearing on the audit on Thursday to discuss the report's findings and recommendations. The D.C. Council has repeatedly called for the District to become more transparent and accountable with its finances. This audit is just the latest example of those concerns. The full audit report is available on the council's website. WTOP's Megan Cloherty contributed to this report. Forecasting is an uncertain venture, even with the use of quantitative methods. This is because the future is inherently uncertain, and the weather is no exception. While quantitative methods can improve our ability to forecast weather, they also have limitations that must be considered. Here we discuss some of the key factors to consider when evaluating the accuracy and limitations of weather forecasts.

## Understanding Forecast Uncertainty
The uncertainty of weather forecasts comes from the chaotic nature of the atmosphere. Small changes in atmospheric conditions can result in large changes in weather patterns over time. This means that even with advanced computer models, forecast uncertainty can be significant, especially when predicting events that are sensitive to small changes in atmospheric conditions, such as a strong or weak storm system.

## Limitations of Quantitative Methods
Quantitative methods for forecasting, such as numerical weather prediction (NWP) models, rely on complex algorithms and large amounts of data. However, even the best NWP models have limitations. These include:
- Model resolution: Higher-resolution models can provide more accurate forecasts, but they also require more computational power and data.
- Model initialization: Forecasts are only as good as the data used to initialize the models. Poor initial conditions can lead to inaccurate forecasts.
- Model complexity: While more complex models can capture more details of the atmosphere, they are also more prone to numerical errors and can be less reliable than simpler models.

## Time and Space Scales
Weather forecasts have different levels of accuracy depending on the time and space scales. Forecasts for short-term events, such as tomorrow's high temperature, are generally more accurate than long-term forecasts, such as predicting next week's weather pattern. Similarly, forecasts for small geographic areas, such as a specific city, are more accurate than those for larger areas, such as a state or region.

## Human Judgment
While quantitative methods can provide useful forecasts, human judgment and expertise are essential for evaluating and interpreting these forecasts. Forecasters must understand the limitations of their models and consider various factors, such as past weather patterns, atmospheric trends, and potential errors, to provide the best possible forecast.

## Conclusion
In summary, forecasting the weather is an uncertain venture, even with the use of quantitative methods. Understanding the uncertainty of weather forecasts and the limitations of quantitative methods is crucial for evaluating the accuracy and reliability of these forecasts. By considering factors such as model resolution, initialization, complexity, time and space scales, and human judgment, we can better understand the potential for errors in weather forecasts and make more informed decisions. ## Dispersion Analysis

Dispersion Analysis是定量诊断中的一个重要工具，用于识别数据之间的变异性及其原因。它可以帮助我们了解数据集的分布特性以及不同变量之间的关系。

### 描述

Dispersion Analysis通常包括三个部分：

1. **中心趋势（Centrality）**：描述数据集的平均值（平均值、均值或中位数）以及数据集的集中趋势（众数）。
2. **分散性（Variability）**：描述数据点之间的距离（数据集的范围或极值）。
3. **协方差（Covariance）**：描述不同变量之间的相关关系。

### Dispersion Analysis的应用

Dispersion Analysis的应用包括：

1. **数据异常检测**：识别数据集中的异常值或 outliers。
2. **数据归纳**：推断出数据集的分布特性（比如说，是否是正态分布或指数分布）。
3. **模型选择**：选择最合适的模型（比如说，决定使用线性模型还是非线性模型）。

### 使用 Dispersion Analysis 实现

Dispersion Analysis通常使用以下统计软件包实现：

1. **R**：使用 `summary()`、`desc()`、`cov()` 和 `var()` 等函数来完成 Dispersion Analysis。
2. **Python**：使用 `numpy`、`pandas` 和 `scipy` 等库来完成 Dispersion Analysis。

Concept of Indian Polity
The journey of Indian polity or the study of Indian government, polity, and politics is an integral part of political science, encompassing various aspects such as power structures, institutions, roles, and processes involved in governing a state or nation. Indian polity evolves from the ancient past to the modern era, involving different phases of state formation, political theories, and institutional developments.
Beginning with the Indus Valley Civilization, Indian polity witnessed various empires and dynasties like the Mauryans, Guptas, and Mughals, each contributing to its developmental trajectory. The concept of polity in India encompassed the East India Company and the eventual emergence of British colonial rule.
India's transition from a colonial to an independent polity was formally achieved on August 15, 1947, with the adoption of the Constitution of India on January 26, 1950. This Constitution serves as the foundation for the Indian polity, providing a detailed outline of the structure of government, powers, and processes of governance, embedding principles of democracy, federalism, secularism, and social justice.
Indian polity is characterized by a federal system of government, a bicameral legislature consisting of the Rajya Sabha and the Lok Sabha, and an independent judiciary with the Supreme Court as its apex. The structure and functions of various constitutional institutions, the principles of equality and justice, and the distribution of power among the central, state, and local governments are all part of the Indian polity framework.

**Key Aspects of Indian Polity:**

1.  **Federal System of Government**: India follows a federal system where power is divided between the center and the states with certain powers reserved to the states and the center.
2.  **Separation of Powers**: The government in India is divided into three branches: legislative, executive, and judiciary, each having defined powers and functions to ensure checks and balances.
3.  **Separation of Church and State**: India is a secular country, with no official state religion, ensuring equal rights and protection to all citizens regardless of their religion.
4.  **Elections and Democracy**: India holds regular elections, and the outcome of these elections determines the political power structure, implementing democratic principles.
5.  **Role of Judiciary**: The Indian judiciary has the power to interpret the Constitution and ensure that the other branches of government remain within their constitutional limits.
6.  **Code of Conduct for Government Servants**: The Government of India has issued a Code of Conduct

=== Guidelines for preparing CTICM data for publication

### Summary

CTICMs provide a rich format for documenting and sharing multiprotein assembly data. However, the provided GOS format of the CTICM representation can be difficult to read. We here document a simple protocol for preparing CTICM data for publication. By automating the data processing, this approach facilitates rapid dissemination and comparison of high-throughput CTICM data.

### Background

CTICMs describe the intra-molecular structure of a protein complex at different stages of its assembly. These structures are typically represented in the GOS (Generic Object Service) format.

### Guidelines

When preparing CTICM data for publication, we recommend the following guidelines.

1. **Select an interaction**:

    Select the interaction you are interested in. You can use the Cytoscape Plugin to view the CTICM data as a network. Alternatively, you can use a GOS parser to load the GOS file and select the relevant interaction.

2. **Protein selection**:

    Select the proteins involved in the interaction.

3. **Partner proteins**:

    Identify the proteins on the opposite side of the interaction.

4. **Use a GOS parser**:

    Use a GOS parser to load the selected interaction.

5. **Paritioning the GOS data**:

    Use a GOS parser to partition the CTICM data into a smaller dataset of protein-protein interactions.

6. **Use open-source tools**:

    Use open-source tools to visualize, extract and process the data.

7. **Data organization**:

    Organize the data into a well-defined structure.

8. **Create visualization**:

    Create a clear visualization of the interaction.

9. **Timing**:

    Give enough time to realize the full potential of the data.

The U.S. Coast Guard ended its last Loran-C station in the Atlantic Ocean in 2010, a few years after ending Loran-C transmission over the Pacific Ocean. The demise of Loran-C was seen as a milestone in the nation's shift towards GPS technology. In reality, both systems coexist today, although GPS is used for navigation purposes more often.
Since the first GPS satellite was launched in 1978, the U.S. Department of Defense has been working on developing navigation technology. Today, the Global Positioning System (GPS), the European Space Agency's Galileo, and China's BeiDou are the leading navigation systems. Satellites orbit the Earth in geostationary orbit, which means that, relative to an observer on the Earth, their movement in the sky does not change much.
GPS is an American space-based navigation system. It consists of three segments: the space segment (containing 24 operational satellites), the control segment (including five monitor stations and three ground antennas), and the user segment (consisting of GPS receivers).
Galileo is the second-generation European satellite navigation system. Its initial operational capability is expected to be available in 2025. Galileo is a global system that provides a 50 times faster time error signal and improved geolocation accuracy compared to GPS.
BeiDou is a Chinese navigation satellite system that provides a global coverage, allowing for seamless tracking and mapping. BeiDou began launching satellites in 2000 and was made operational for maritime use in 2012. BeiDou provides more precise positioning, wider coverage, and better anti-jamming capabilities.
Despite their successes, the limitations of these satellite navigation systems should be acknowledged. For instance, they may not operate in locations where signals are obstructed, such as inside dense forests, buildings, or under mountainous terrain. In such cases, other navigation systems, like Loran-C, could still be utilized. However, Loran-C is vulnerable to electromagnetic interference, which reduces its effectiveness.
Innovative navigation technologies, such as augmented reality and instrument landing systems, are being developed to address these limitations. Augmented reality allows pilots to navigate by projecting virtual overlays of information on a real environment. Instrument landing systems use a localizer system and a glide slope system to guide aircraft during the final approach.

# Ramdhenu Devi

Ramdhenu Devi (Sanskrit: रामधेनु देवी, romanized: Rāmadhenu Devī, lit. 'Cow Goddess of Sita') is a goddess in Hindu mythology and the wife of Krisna, the avatar of Vishnu. Her original name is believed to be Matsya, in the Matsya Purana, but is given the name Ramdhenu Devi by Valmiki Ramayana.

It seems like you're asking about the grammatical verb forms in Korean and the differences in verb conjugation between each form. Specifically, you're looking at the verb conjugation in the "감" (cru) form and how it compares to the other potential grammatical forms.

I'll summarize the main differences in the following four forms:

1. Plain form:
   The plain form is the basic form of a verb in the present tense.
2. Nominal form:
   This form is used when the verb is used as a noun. Its conjugation is the same as the infinitive form.
3. Conjunctive form (comma):
   This form is used to connect two clauses. Its conjugation is the same as the nom/indicative form (the suffix "-" replaces the suffix "-")
4. Causal form (gam):
   This form is used to indicate a reason or cause. Its conjugation is different from the other forms (specifically, it takes the "e", "geoseyo" and "-nun" ending)
5. Assimilated form:
   This form is a set of rules for specific irregular verb conjugations.

So, to answer your question, the '감' (cru) form has different verb conjugation rules compared to the other forms. Unlike the "comma" form, the "gam" form takes the "-e" and "-geoseyo" ending, and the irregular conjugations in the "gam" form can be quite complex.

The German settlement of Walhalla was founded in 1858. It is now a ghost town. A large number of German settlers arrived between 1848 and 1852. They were mainly Lutherans. Over 60% of the settlers came from the vicinity of Berlin. They came as 200 migrants who were mainly farmers and 200 other Germans and British who were laborers or were in the church.
When the Lutheran church was opened in 1858 the town was known as Lucknow. In 1859 the town was renamed to Walhalla after the mythological North American Valley of gold. This however meant that there were two towns with similar names. The competing gold rush town of Saint's Lucknow which was only a few kilometers away chose to call itself Walhalla instead of Saint's Lucknow.
Saint's Lucknow has since become a part of the nearby town of Hawker which is the main town in the Strzelecki Desert.
In 1870 it was decided that Walhalla should be renamed. It was changed back to Lucknow and then in 1879 was renamed to Orroroo. The new name of Orroroo gave rise to more confusion as Saint's Lucknow was still around. Thus it is better to use the name Hawker and Saint's Lucknow to avoid confusion.
Today Hawker is still used as the main town for the area. The town of Orroroo is often confused with the nearby park Orroroo Springs.
Saint's Lucknow can be found 32 km north of Hawker just off the A32 Stuart Highway. You have to cross the Willochra Creek to enter Saint's Lucknow.
The site of Lucknow has become an historic reserve.
There are still remnants of the lucknow Lutheran church nearby. The full story of the church is to be found on its wall.
Another historic site in Saint's Lucknow is the site of the school.

Static and Non-Static Variables in Python
Python Variables
Variables in Python can be either static or non-static.
Static Variable (Class Variable)
A class variable in Python is also known as a static variable. It is a variable that belongs to the class rather than to an instance of the class. It is a common variable that can be shared by all instances of a class. It is declared outside of any method but inside the class.
Static variables must be prefixed with the class name followed by a dot.
Declaring Static Variable:
In Python, we declare a static variable by using the class name followed by the dot operator.
``` 
class Student:
    students_count = 0
    def __init__(self, name):
        self.name = name
        Student.students_count += 1
```
Accessing Static Variable:
To access a static variable, we use the class name followed by the dot operator.
``` 
s = Student("John")
print(Student.students_count)  # Outputs: 1
```
Non-Static Variable (Instance Variable)
A non-static variable in Python is also known as an instance variable. It is a variable that belongs to an instance of the class. It is a variable that holds the unique value for each object.
Instance variables are variables that are declared inside a method and they are used to store values that are specific to an instance of the class.
Declaring Non-Static Variable:
In Python, we declare an instance variable by using the self keyword.
``` 
class Student:
    def __init__(self, name):
        self.name = name
```
Accessing Non-Static Variable:
To access an instance variable, we use the instance followed by the dot operator.
``` 
s = Student("John")
print(s.name)  # Outputs: John
```
Difference between Static and Non-Static Variables:
The main difference between static and non-static variables in Python is:
1.  **Scope**: The scope of a static variable is the entire class, while the scope of a non-static variable is the instance of the class.
2.  **Accessibility**: Static variables are accessible using the class name, while non-static variables are accessible using the instance.
3.  **Initialization**: Static variables are initialized when the class is loaded, while non-static variables are initialized when an instance of the class is created.

The Faculty of Education at Monash University acknowledges the need for effective strategies to prevent and respond to workplace bullying, which is a significant concern for employees and employers in the higher education sector. The Australian Human Rights Commission's (AHRC) Inquiry into Workplace Bullying presents an opportunity to inform national policy and practice. Below, we provide our submission in response to the AHRC's discussion paper.
In preparing this submission, we drew on feedback from our staff members and stakeholders, as well as our existing workplace bullying policy and procedures. We believe our submission highlights the importance of prevention, education and support in reducing workplace bullying in higher education institutions.
Submissions to the Australian Human Rights Commission’s Inquiry into Workplace Bullying
Overall, the AHRC's Inquiry provides a vital opportunity to examine the prevalence and impact of workplace bullying in Australia, and to develop evidence-based strategies to prevent and address it.
We have focused on responding to questions related to prevention, education and support, as these are key components in reducing workplace bullying in higher education institutions.
1. Prevention
Workplace bullying often occurs due to a combination of factors, including poor communication, inadequate leadership, and inadequate policies and procedures (Hansen et al., 2019). In our submission, we argue that the key components of a preventative approach to workplace bullying in higher education institutions include:
A clear policy that defines workplace bullying, the behaviours it entails, and how to report incidents;
Training and education programs for all staff members on workplace bullying, its consequences, and how to prevent it;
Inclusive leadership practices, including fostering a culture of respect and empathy, and modelling positive behaviours;
Regular monitoring and review of workplace bullying policies and procedures to ensure their effectiveness.

This summer, Minnesota’s weather has been a hot mess with temperatures soaring above 90 degrees with an oppressive humidity. But that doesn’t stop Rachel Kang, an Eagan mother of two, from planning a unique event to raise awareness and funds for neurodegenerative diseases like Alzheimer’s. With the support of her family and friends, Rachel has started CLEO'S memory project, an innovative endeavor that combines art, community, and fundraising.
I recently visited Rachel’s home in Eagan, where CLEO – the lovable Shiba Inu – was seated regally in the backyard, enjoying the shade beneath a colorful umbrella. Rachel explained to me the story behind CLEO'S memory project and how her beloved pet became the inspiration.
Rachel’s grandmother, Daisy, passed away in 2018 due to complications related to Alzheimer’s disease. Shortly after, Rachel received devastating news that her father would soon be losing his battle with the same condition. It was during this period of grief that Rachel decided to honor Daisy and her father by starting CLEO'S memory project.
CLEO, her loyal Shiba Inu companion, was instrumental in giving Rachel the idea for the project. While out on walks with CLEO, Rachel met many people who shared their personal stories about loved ones with Alzheimer’s or other neurodegenerative diseases. CLEO became the unexpected ambassador for the cause, captivating people with her charm and winning over their hearts.
The project began with CLEO'S armchair, a tastefully designed wooden rocking chair adorned with the names of individuals who have passed away due to neurodegenerative diseases. Rachel, with the help of her family and friends, has set up the armchair in the backyard of her home for public view. Visitors can take a photo with CLEO and pay a visit to the armchair, which has become a poignant tribute to the lives of those who have been lost

Social Services program helping thousands in Florida
TALLAHASSEE – The state of Florida’s Temporary Assistance for Needy Families (TANF) program has provided financial assistance to over 100,000 low-income families in the last fiscal year.
The program, funded by the federal government and administered by the Agency for Health Care Administration (AHCA), helps families with children pay for things like housing, food and other basic needs.
"Florida's TANF program helps some of our most vulnerable citizens - families with children who are struggling to make ends meet," AHCA Secretary Justin Senior said. "By providing them with the financial support they need, we can help them achieve self-sufficiency and stability."
In addition to financial assistance, the program also provides services like food assistance, childcare assistance, and employment and job training.
"We're not just giving people a handout; we're giving them a helping hand up," Senior said. "We want to help families become more independent and self-sufficient, and by doing so, we're helping to create a stronger, more prosperous community for everyone."
Of the over 100,000 families assisted by the program in the last fiscal year, nearly 60 percent were from households with children under the age of 18. The average TANF benefit amount for these families was around $185 per month.
The state also reported that the number of families served by the program increased by about 11 percent compared to the previous fiscal year.
Florida's TANF program serves not only families with children but also pregnant women, infants and children under the age of six who are at risk of being neglected or abused.
TANF program rules require families to work at least 30 hours per week or participate in work-related activities. Additionally, families are required to be enrolled in job training or education programs for at least 30 hours per week to be eligible for continued TANF benefits. -30-

Autoimmune diseases occur when the body's immune system mistakenly attacks healthy tissues, organs, or cells. In the case of rheumatoid arthritis (RA), the immune system targets the lining of the joints, known as synovium, causing pain, inflammation, and swelling. As the disease progresses, the synovium can thicken and cartilage can break down, leading to joint damage and permanent deformity.
Recent research suggests that RA is caused by an abnormal immune response, specifically the production of autoantibodies that target the rheumatoid factor (RF) protein, which is present in the joints. This protein is actually produced by the immune system, but in RA patients, it becomes targeted by their own immune cells, leading to inflammation and joint damage.
Researchers are working to develop new treatments that can prevent or reverse this autoimmune response and restore balance to the immune system. Several promising approaches include:
1. Tofacitinib: This oral medication has been shown to block the action of certain immune cells, reducing inflammation and slowing disease progression.
2. Baricitinib: Another oral medication, baricitinib has been shown to be effective in reducing inflammation and improving symptoms in patients with RA.
3. Anti-TNF (tumor necrosis factor) therapies: Medications like etanercept (Enbrel) and adalimumab (Humira) work by blocking the action of TNF, a protein that promotes inflammation.
4. Biologics: These medications target specific proteins involved in the immune response, such as interleukin-6 (IL-6) and interleukin-1 beta (IL-1β).
5. Gene therapy: Scientists are exploring ways to modify or replace genes involved in the immune response, potentially reducing the risk of developing RA or slowing its progression.
6. Stem cell therapy: Researchers are investigating the use of stem cells to repair damaged joints and promote healing.
7. Medications targeting IL-17: This protein is produced by immune cells and has been linked to the development of RA. Medications like secukinumab (Cosentyx) and ixekizumab (Taltz) are being developed to block its action.
8. Rapamycin: This medication, also known as sirolimus, has been shown to reduce inflammation and prevent the production of autoantibodies in animal models of RA.

These emerging treatments hold promise for patients with RA, but more research is needed to fully understand their effectiveness and potential side effects. Your healthcare

Palau: Resilience in the face of adversity
It’s just a month since Cyclone Haima battered Palau in the Pacific Ocean, leaving widespread destruction and a trail of devastation in its wake. The small Pacific Island nation has long been recognised for its rich marine ecosystem and commitment to conservation, but now it faces an even greater challenge – to rebuild and recover from the aftermath of the cyclone.
The storm made landfall on 20 October and then swept through the islands on 21 October, bringing with it category 5 winds and torrential rain. Palau reported its first direct hit by a cyclone in 25 years, and it was the most powerful to have struck the country in recorded history. The impact was catastrophic: 90% of the infrastructure in the northern state of Melekeok was destroyed, the cost of which is estimated to be over $150 million.
As with every disaster, there are lessons to be learned, and the resilience of Palau stands out in the face of adversity. On the international stage, Palau has been an important player in global conservation efforts, protecting its marine environment and pushing for ambitious targets to be set to mitigate the effects of climate change. In fact, Palau is often cited as one of the countries that have shown remarkable leadership in sustainable development and resilience, earning recognition from the United Nations General Assembly for its contributions to achieving the Sustainable Development Goals.
In Palau, resilience is not just a concept – it's a way of life. The country's traditional values, including the concept of ulechelcheil, or living with nature, guide its people in managing resources and working together to overcome adversity. At a time when many countries are struggling to respond to the consequences of climate change, Palau shows that there are examples to be learned from a country that has made a bold commitment to protecting the world’s biodiversity.
Efforts are underway to rebuild the country and assist the people affected by the cyclone. International assistance from UN agencies, NGOs and government partners is vital, but so too is the Palauan people's own resilience and spirit in the face of disaster.

Managing expenses is a crucial task for non-profit organizations, where every dollar counts. Non-profit expense tracking software can help streamline this process, ensuring accurate and transparent financial management. Here are some key features and considerations for non-profit expense tracking software:

Key Features:

1.  **Expense categorization**: The ability to categorize expenses by type, such as travel, program expenses, or administrative costs, to simplify reporting and analysis.
2.  **Reimbursement workflows**: A system for submitting and approving expenses, ensuring that reimbursement requests are handled efficiently and accurately.
3.  **Integration with accounting systems**: Seamless integration with popular accounting software, such as QuickBooks or Xero, to eliminate duplicate data entry and ensure financial accuracy.
4.  **Reporting and analytics**: The capacity to generate reports on expenses, income, and financial performance, helping non-profits make informed decisions.
5.  **Security and compliance**: Robust security measures and compliance with financial regulations, such as GDPR and CCPA, to protect sensitive financial data.
6.  **Mobile accessibility**: A mobile-friendly interface, allowing users to submit and approve expenses on-the-go.

Considerations:

1.  **Customization**: The ability to tailor the expense tracking software to the non-profit's specific needs and financial structure.
2.  **Scalability**: The software's ability to grow with the organization, accommodating increased volume and complexity.
3.  **Training and support**: Access to comprehensive training, documentation, and customer support to ensure a smooth implementation and troubleshooting process.
4.  **Cost**: The total cost of ownership, including subscription fees, implementation costs, and any additional expenses for customizations or support.
5.  **Data storage**: The security and accessibility of financial data, including storage in a secure, cloud-based environment.

3.  **Zoho Expense**: A cloud-based expense tracking software with a comprehensive feature set, including mobile accessibility, customizable workflows, and integration with popular accounting systems.

C. 促进肝脏糖原分解

选项B表示胰岛素可以促进脂肪酸的合成，但是这种说法是错误的。实际上，胰岛素可以促进脂肪酸的分解。

选项C表示胰岛素可以促进肝脏糖原分解，但是这也是错误的。胰岛素实际上是促进糖原合成和氯离子和钾离子保留的。

选项D表示胰岛素可以促进蛋白质合成，这是正确的。胰岛素能够促进蛋白质合成并有助于细胞存活。

选项E表示胰岛素可以促进氯离子和钾离子的排泄，这是错误的。胰岛素实际上可以促进钾离子的保留并有助于维持体内正电平衡。

Psychology, particularly child psychology, is an increasingly important area of research in today’s society. Children’s behavior and cognitive development are crucial factors in understanding how they learn, interact with the world, and navigate social situations.
As technology plays an ever-larger role in our lives, more and more research focuses on how children interact with digital media, and how this affects their behavior, learning, and development.
One significant area of research is how technology affects children’s social and emotional development. Studies have explored the impact of digital media on children’s social skills, empathy, and emotional regulation, often finding that excessive digital media use is linked to negative outcomes, such as decreased empathy and increased symptoms of anxiety and depression.
Child Psychology research also examines the role of technology in children’s cognitive development, including their learning habits, attention span, and problem-solving skills. Some studies investigate how digital media, such as video games and educational apps, can be designed to support cognitive development, promoting skills like critical thinking and spatial reasoning.
Child Psychology research often focuses on understanding the environmental factors that influence children’s behavior and development. These include family dynamics, socioeconomic status, and access to resources such as education and healthcare.
Some researchers investigate how technology can be used to support children’s mental health, particularly in the face of challenges such as bullying, anxiety, or trauma. This might involve the development of digital interventions, such as online therapy platforms or social support groups.
In conclusion, child psychology is an important area of research that seeks to understand the complexities of childhood development and behavior. The impact of technology on children’s lives is a key area of focus, and ongoing research aims to inform the development of evidence-based interventions and policies that support children’s well-being and development.

dentures If you have one or more missing teeth, you may need dentures. At Advanced Dental Care of West Orange, we provide affordable and durable dentures to replace your missing teeth. Our dentist will evaluate your oral health and recommend the best option for your teeth replacement needs.
There are several types of dentures, including:
Conventional Dentures: These are removable dentures that are custom-made for your mouth. They are a common choice for patients who have lost most or all of their natural teeth.
Immediate Dentures: These dentures are created and placed in your mouth on the same day as the tooth extraction. They help to minimize the appearance of your missing teeth and support your healing gums.
Partial Dentures: These dentures are used when some natural teeth are still present. They fill the gaps and restore your ability to chew and speak.
Overdentures: These dentures are fitted over natural teeth and used to replace missing teeth. They provide additional stability and support for your dentures.
