A 41-year-old Illinois teacher has been arrested and charged with multiple counts of arson after police alleged he burned down several schools to collect the insurance money.
According to a statement from the police department, Rockford school teacher LeVasseur Curtis, a sixth-grade language arts teacher at Spring Creek Elementary, is accused of setting fires at three separate schools in the Rockford School District: Lane Elementary, Green Thermal Skye Elementary, and Papasp Handbooksisen Elementary.
Police said that on Tuesday, July 18, authorities received reports of a fire at Lane Elementary. As they investigated, they discovered that the blaze started in an empty classroom and spread to other parts of the building, causing an estimated $2 million in damages. Investigators discovered that the fire had a suspicious origin and launched an investigation.
As the investigation continued, police found evidence that Curtis had started two other fires in the Rockford School District. Green Thermal Skye Elementary suffered an estimated $3 million in damage on July 16, and Papasp Handbooksisen Elementary sustained an estimated $1 million in damage on July 20.
The motive behind the alleged arson spree, police alleged, was the collection of insurance money. While Rockford School District officials declined to comment on Curtis's employment status, his contract was slated to expire on August 31.
Curtis was arrested on August 10, two days after the Papasp Handbooksisen Elementary fire, and charged with five counts of arson and two counts of unlawful possession of fire.
Illinois authorities also discovered that Curtis had previously worked at an auto insurance firm and that he had applied for a series of insurance policies in recent months, covering both his home and several school buildings in the Rockford School District.
While authorities have not disclosed the exact amount Curtis was seeking in insurance proceeds, they allege he intended to collect the payments for multiple school fires.
Curtis is being held at the Winnebago County Jail on a $5 million bond. Prosecutors are seeking to keep him behind bars until his trial.

The City of Vancouver is increasing the number of permitted rooming houses and affordable housing units in neighbourhoods across the city. The changes are a response to the growing need for affordable housing, particularly for low-income households, seniors, and Indigenous peoples. Starting July 2023, eligible rooming houses will be able to increase their maximum occupancy from one to four units, and in high-demand areas, even more units may be allowed. The changes also make it easier to convert other types of properties into rooming houses, including those previously underutilized for decades. The new regulations make it easier to convert other types of properties into rooming houses. This can include:

Some of the ways that living organisms obtain and utilize energy are unique. For example, photosynthesis in green plants results in chemical energy, in the form of carbohydrates, being synthesized from sunlight and carbon dioxide. When this product is oxidized (using oxygen in the process), an organism obtains chemical energy. This process of oxidation of carbohydrates is not unique to humans or animals. Organisms at the base of the food pyramid, like fungi and algae, are unable to obtain energy from sunlight directly like green plants; therefore, they are unable to provide themselves with the chemical energy their cells need to survive. These organisms convert inorganic carbon, like carbon dioxide, to a usable form by reducing it to organic carbon, like glucose.
Plants and animals that obtain their energy by eating other organisms are said to be _heterotrophic_. In contrast, organisms like green plants, which use sunlight for chemical energy, are called _autotrophic_. Chemically speaking, autotrophic organisms consume CO\({}_{2}\) to produce glucose, which in turn is a source of energy.
## Energy, an important concept in the study of living organisms
Living organisms use energy in a great variety of ways, just as do inorganic systems. Energy must be obtained, and this energy must be efficiently used. Unused energy is wasted, just as "wasted" is a word often used to describe an impulsive or unethical act. Metabolic processes require _energy_, and living organisms _need_ energy to _survive_. But what is an _energy need_?
### Energy needs of living organisms
There is one inevitable energy requirement of all living organisms--to obtain energy. An _energy need_ occurs when some biological function requires an additional quantity of energy. The _metabolism_ of an organism is subject to the same laws of conservation and energy availability that inorganic systems obey.

Details about Functional Indeterminacy of Moral Terms
This book examines the metaphysics of moral statements. Walter Ettinger argues that moral statements are best seen as concerning functions that pick out our moral terms rather than the properties themselves to which those terms refer. He claims that the reference of moral terms is indeterminate, not due to ontological vagueness, but due to a linguistic phenomenon - the multiple realizability of functions. Functions can be realized by different properties, and this indeterminacy of reference is what makes moral statements truth-apt. Ettinger's metaphysical analysis has important implications for the epistemology of moral claims. He defends a kind of moral realism that claims that objective moral facts can be known, despite the indeterminacy of moral reference.

Police have charged four suspects with possession of an explosive device, following a report of a suspicious item found in a vehicle on Wednesday afternoon.
Around 2pm, police were called to a car parked in a vehicle park on Glasgow Road in Coatbridge, North Lanarkshire.
The driver reported that a suspicious item had been discovered in the vehicle and officers attended the scene to carry out an investigation.
Bomb disposal experts were also called to the area and a cordon was put in place to ensure public safety.
After conducting an examination, police confirmed that the item was an explosive device, but it had not been activated and posed no immediate threat.
Now, four men, aged 24, 26, 31 and 33, have been charged in connection with the incident. They are due to appear at Airdrie Sheriff Court on Monday.
Detective Chief Inspector Colin Hiddleston said: “The charge of possession of an explosive device is a serious one, and these four men now face a substantial amount of work and investigation as we build the case against them.
“Our focus has always been on the safety of the public, and I would like to thank the local community for their patience and cooperation while we carried out our work.
“Although the item in question did not pose an immediate threat, it was still a significant concern, and the public can be reassured that we treated the situation with the utmost seriousness. 
“An investigation is ongoing, and I would like to appeal to anyone who may have information about the incident to come forward and speak to us. We will leave no stone unturned in our efforts to build the case and bring those responsible to justice.” 
Anyone with information can contact the police on 101 or Crimestoppers on 0800 555 111.

Air Force Association Announces the 2020 Lieutenant General Barbara G. Larkin Award
The Air Force Association (AFA) announced the 2020 Lieutenant General Barbara G. Larkin Award will be presented to Amanda Lynn Barnes, Chief, Air Force Civil Engineer Center – Utility Systems, Tyndall Air Force Base, Florida.
The award recognizes career field professionals, both military and civilian, who have significantly contributed to and improved the Air Force’s installation support services within their area of specialty.
Barnes was selected for the award due to her unwavering commitment to the Air Force’s utility system programs and her tireless efforts to revitalize the service’s capability to provide electrical power, water, and waste management to our bases and allies.
Over the years, Barnes has been instrumental in developing innovative solutions to support combat and disaster response operations. Her tireless efforts have saved millions of dollars and in the process, improved the service’s operational effectiveness.
This is not the first time Barnes has received recognition for her hard work and dedication. Josef Bartoschek (1891-1977) - SS-Obersturmführer
Josef Bartoschek was born on October 28, 1891, in Berlin, Germany, and joined the army in 1909 at the age of 18. He served in the war until 1918 and was promoted to Leutnant. In 1933 he joined the NSDAP and on August 10, 1936, he became a member of the SS (SS-Nummer: 285370).
In May 1936 he transferred to the SS-Verfügungstruppe, and in November 1936, he was assigned as Adjutant in the Stab of the Leibstandarte SS Adolf Hitler (LSSAH). He was promoted to Untersturmführer on September 9, 1937, and on June 21, 1941, he was promoted to Obersturmführer.
The first military commitment of the LSSAH was the invasion of Poland, where LSSAH distinguished itself. From May 1940, the LSSAH was involved in the invasion of France. The success of these campaigns was to a significant extent due to the excellence of the tactical ideas and methods of their leader, SA-Obergruppenführer Josef ("Sepp") Dietrich.
In May 1940, Bartoschek was placed in charge of intelligence and counter-intelligence for the entire LSSAH. He was not a capable leader, but as a reliable "old comrade" (altkampfer), he was in favor with Sepp Dietrich, who had no alternative choice, rather than to use some more talented SS personnel.
After the start of Operation Barbarossa (the invasion of the Soviet Union) in June 1941, Bartoschek participated with the LSSAH in several operations in the north of the Eastern Front. In January 1943, he was decorated with the Deutsches Kreuz in Gold (Diamond) by Hitler personally for his "brilliant military achievements".
Josef Bartoschek was severely wounded on April 5, 1943, during the battles of the LSSAH near Lake Ilmen. He was captured by the Soviet forces and later repatriated to Germany. This event did not just affect the physical landscape, but also challenged the existing social hierarchy and cultural practices. Are they feasible for anyone, or is this something reserved for those with boundless wealth? We’re breaking down the costs of Round the World trips to give you an idea of what to expect.
We have to address the elephant in the room: the costs of Round the World (RTW) travel are significant. They can, however, be managed with careful planning and research. It's not just about saving up; understanding how to plan your RTW trip will make a significant difference in your expenses.
Cost Structure:
Several factors contribute to the overall costs of RTW travel:
1. Transportation Costs: One of the significant expenses is flights. Different types of travel and accommodations can affect prices:
    * **Bus passes (e.g., Greyhound):** Can be very affordable but offer limited routes and flexibility.
    * **Budget airlines:** Frequents flights but may require more time and transfers, increasing travel time.
    * **Trains and overnight buses:** Offer a different travel experience, often suitable for shorter distances within continents.
    * **Flight passes (e.g., Eurail, Eurail RAIL PASS):** Best value for specific regions but limit the type of trains you can take.
2. Accommodation Costs: This depends on your travel style:
    * **Hostels and budget hotels:** Cost-effective, with dorm rooms and private rooms available.
    * **Mid-range hotels:** More comfortable but pricier.
    * **Luxury hotels:** Only for those on a high-end budget.
    * **Homestays and short-term rentals:** Offers a more immersive experience but with varying price tags.
3. Food and Activities: These costs add up quickly:
    * **Budget eating:** Experience local cuisine, but be prepared for unique flavors and, sometimes, questionable hygiene.
    * **Mid-range restaurants:** A better taste and ambiance but may cost more.
    * **Experience-centric travel:** Worth it for memorable experiences but, in some cases, quite expensive.
4. Miscellaneous Expenses:
    * **Visas:** A complex process with fees for some countries; this should be factored in early.
    * **Travel insurance:** Protect yourself from unexpected events but add up in costs.
    * **Other costs:** Vaccinations, luggage fees, and gear expenses can accumulate.

def harvest_crop(crop_name, yield_amount):
    """
    This function simulates the harvesting of a crop.

    Args:
    crop_name (str): The name of the crop being harvested.
    yield_amount (float): The amount of the crop that is being harvested.

    Returns:
    A message indicating the crop has been successfully harvested.
    """

    # First, we need to check if the crop name is a string.
    # If it's not, we raise a TypeError with a descriptive message.
    if not isinstance(crop_name, str):
        raise TypeError("Crop name must be a string.")

    # Next, we need to check if the yield amount is a number.
    # If it's not, we raise a TypeError with a descriptive message.
    if not isinstance(yield_amount, (int, float)):
        raise TypeError("Yield amount must be a number.")

    # Now that we've validated our inputs, we can proceed with the harvest.
    # We print a message to confirm the harvest is taking place.
    print(f"Harvesting {crop_name} crop...")

    # Next, we simulate the harvesting process by sleeping for a short period.

    import time
    time.sleep(1)

    # Now that the harvest is complete, we print a confirmation message.
    print(f"{crop_name} crop has been successfully harvested with a yield of {yield_amount} units.")

    # Finally, we return a message indicating the crop has been harvested.
    return f"{crop_name} crop has been harvested."

摘要： 本文是关于高压蒸汽灭菌对蛋白质激酶的影响的研究报告。本研究利用高压蒸汽灭菌对多种蛋白质激酶进行试验，并探讨了灭菌过程中蛋白质激酶活性的变化。本文显示，高压蒸汽灭菌对蛋白质激酶有影响，灭菌过程中的高温、高压和动力学有助于蛋白质激酶的降解和失活。因此，高压蒸汽灭菌对蛋白质激酶的影响值得进一步研究和探讨，以保证研究中的样品质量和分析准确性。
Abstract： This study investigated the effects of high pressure steam sterilization on protein kinases. Protein kinases from various sources were subjected to high pressure steam sterilization to examine the impact of sterilization on their activity. Our results indicate that sterilization leads to degradation and inactivation of the enzymes. The high temperature, pressure and dynamics involved in the sterilization process may account for the observed effects. These findings suggest that high pressure steam sterilization has an impact on protein kinases that warrants further study to ensure the quality and accuracy of analyses in research settings.

Design of an Edge-Selective Method to Build Graphene-Based Sensors
Keywords: graphene, sensors, edge-selective functionalization, molecular detection, sensor architectures
Abstract: Graphene-based sensors with tunable and programmable sensitivity and selectivity are of prime interest for the development of ultra-sensitive sensors for a wide variety of applications, including detection of biomolecules and environmental pollutants. One critical challenge to achieve highly sensitive and selective sensing is the efficient functionalization of graphene with the desired sensing motifs, such as fluorescent, electrochemical or biofunctional units. Here, we propose a novel method to build graphene-based sensors via edge-selective functionalization. This method allows creating in situ tailor-made graphene networks or single sheets with programmed properties, combining modularity, precision and scalability. The approach relies on the design of nanometer-scale heterogeneities at the graphene edge, which can be used as a supramolecular platform for selectively binding target species. Our approach represents a paradigm shift in the realization of graphene-based sensors, offering a new degree of freedom in material design and rendering them attractive for various sensing applications.

In physics, we use mathematics and theoretical frameworks to understand the world. As the bus approached the city, the pavement started to get rougher. People moved quickly on the sidewalk, dodging around each other as they went about their day. Emily felt a twinge of guilt for not being a part of this flow of people. She had a job, just like everyone else, but it felt like an afterthought. She didn’t know what else to do with herself, so she trudged along, day after day.
The bus hit a pothole, making Emily jolt forward in her seat. She let out a reflexive yelp, startling the man sitting next to her. He gave her a sympathetic smile and went back to staring out his own window. Emily felt a flutter of gratitude. For a moment, she forgot about the weight of her own existence and just felt a connection to this stranger.
They rode the rest of the way in silence, but Emily felt a sense of hope stirring inside her. She didn’t have to be alone with her thoughts, not when there were other people out there. She could connect with them, if she just let herself. The bus pulled up to her stop, and Emily stood up, feeling a sense of resolve wash over her. Today might not be the best day, but she was ready for whatever came next. And who knows, maybe it would be better than she thought. The past few days have been a whirlwind of Italy. We've been crisscrossing the country, visiting fashion houses, artisans, and old friends. Today we stopped in Maranello, home of Ferrari, the ultimate expression of Italian style and passion.
We spent the morning driving a fabulous little Ferrari, twisting and turning through the countryside in a whirlwind of speed and fun. Our instructor, Andrea, was a former racing driver with a penchant for getting us out of every hairpin turn with speed and style. We learned a lot about the handling and performance of this incredible machine, but more importantly, we had a blast.
We met some of the Ferrari team members, including an engineer who showed us the Formula One cars and explained how they're built. It's incredible to think that these cars, which can reach speeds of over 200 miles per hour, are built by hand in this small town in Italy.
After lunch, we took a tour of the Ferrari museum, which is a must-see for any car enthusiast. The collection includes some of the most iconic Ferraris of all time, including the Daytona, the 250 GT, and the Enzo. It's an incredible display of style, craftsmanship, and passion.
Tonight, we're enjoying a lovely dinner at our hotel, which is a restored 19th-century villa with beautiful gardens and a swimming pool. We're reflecting on the amazing experiences we've had today and the incredible beauty of this country. It's been a truly unforgettable day, and we're so grateful to have had this adventure. Tomorrow, we head to the north of Italy to visit the fashion capital of Milan. Can't wait to see what tomorrow brings! Buon giorno, Italy!

Barrier: Dilemmas in humanitarian aid delivery PDF Print E-mail
Directing aid distribution to those in need is complex, especially in situations where governments are not in control, or when there are political, military or religious interests at play. These dilemmas have been well documented in a new book by the Centre on Conflict, Development and Peacebuilding (CCDP) of the Graduate Institute of International and Development Studies in Geneva.
Edited by Oliver P. Richmond, Maren Bode, Pontus Østerman and Tasha Siddali, "After Intervention: Public – Private Partnerships in Peacebuilding" discusses the implications of humanitarian intervention and public – private partnerships in fragile or conflict-affected areas. The authors point out the main challenges in aid delivery in such complex contexts, where public and private partners are often in disagreement about priorities, goals and methods.
The ten case studies presented in the book focus on concrete situations, from Somalian peacekeeping efforts to delivery of international aid in Iraq, and from Islamist influences on relief efforts in Bosnia-Herzegovina to Russian-backed efforts in Georgia.
"One of the main contradictions is that public partners, like governments and international institutions, want to exercise control and direct how aid is delivered, but private partners, like NGOs and businesspeople, push for greater autonomy and faster decision-making," explains Miriam J. Cunningham, of the CCDP.
By presenting case studies of both successful and unsuccessful humanitarian interventions, the book identifies that overall aid delivery remains reactive, lacking strategic planning and engaging only isolated communities.
If successful, integrating public and private efforts in such conflict zones can lead to more targeted, needs-based relief and include vital social investment that benefits the most vulnerable populations, increasing resilience and stability. "This is the ultimate goal – sustained peace-building," as described by Marie-Laure Nodon of CGAP (Consultative Group to Assist the Poor).
Yet, when partnerships falter, results can be short-lived and insufficient, producing a range of negative effects, including human rights abuses, decreased community confidence and even increased insecurity in fragile and often humanitarian-dependent areas.
CCDP's comprehensive study is revealing on how previously established international guidelines and mechanisms should be reevaluated to address these partnerships' multifaceted responsibilities and quality assessments.

A. maybe

Unit: mmol
Explanation: To investigate the relationship between urinary albumin excretion and apoptosis of renal tubular cells in patients with type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM). The apoptosis of renal tubular cells was evaluated by terminal deoxynucleotidyl transferase dUTP nick end labeling (TUNEL) staining and the expression of caspase-3.
A total of 70 patients with T2DM were divided into five groups according to their urinary albumin excretion rates (UAE): normal albuminuria (NA) group (< 20 mg/24 h), microalbuminuria (MA) group (20-200 mg/24 h), macroalbuminuria (MA) group (200-1,000 mg/24 h), overt albuminuria (OA) group (1,000-2,000 mg/24 h), and heavy albuminuria (HA) group (> 2,000 mg/24 h).
The rate of TUNEL-positive cells was significantly higher in the OA and HA groups than in the NA, MA and MA groups (P < 0.05). The expression of caspase-3 was also significantly higher in the OA and HA groups than in the NA, MA and MA groups (P < 0.05). A positive correlation was found between UAE and the rate of TUNEL-positive cells (r = 0.842, P < 0.001). A positive correlation was also found between UAE and the expression of caspase-3 (r = 0.736, P < 0.001).
The relationship between urinary albumin excretion and apoptosis of renal tubular cells in patients with T2DM indicates that increased urinary albumin excretion may be associated with apoptosis of renal tubular cells in patients with T2DM, suggesting that apoptosis of renal tubular cells may play a role in the pathogenesis of diabetic nephropathy. Apoptosis of renal tubular cells could be an early sign of diabetic nephropathy. Keywords: type 2 diabetes mellitus, urinary albumin excretion, apoptosis of renal tubular cells. In the 19th century, the geoduck (a type of large, edible saltwater clam) was prized as a delicacy in the Pacific Northwest, and barnacles (gnathia spp.), which often accompanied geoducks in their shells, were often consumed by locals, like a side dish. In fact, many of the original food ethnographies from the time refer to barnacles as a delicious, chewy, and salty snack.
The geoduck-and-barnacle appetizer was historically a popular treat in coastal Asian, European, and indigenous cultures, and was considered an important food source for many families and communities. So, why did barnacles fall out of favor?
While, in recent years, there has been a renewed interest in foraging for seaweed and wild edibles along the coast, barnacles remain relatively underappreciated. There are a few reasons why they may have been overlooked in recent history, despite their delicious and nutritious qualities:
1. **Limited access**: The early colonial settlers, who introduced European agricultural practices to the region, may have viewed barnacles as undesirable or nuisance animals, rather than a valuable food source. These practices, which focused on dominant livestock species like cattle, sheep, and pigs, may have inadvertently led to the decline of barnacle appreciation.
2. **Economic and cultural context**: For many centuries, the main income-generating industries in the region were fishing and logging, which greatly impacted the forest and marine ecosystems. Fishermen and loggers would prioritize their income-generating activities over foraging, and communities that traditionally foraged for barnacles and geoducks may have shifted their practices to focus on more profitable activities.
3. **Perceived value**: In the 19th century, the European-American diet in the Pacific Northwest favored a focus on meat, bread, and potatoes, with seafood considered a luxury. In this context, geoducks and barnacles, although prized by coastal populations, were often seen as inferior to land-based meats and grains.
4. **Loss of traditional knowledge and skills**: As traditional coastal communities assimilated into mainstream culture, many of the skills and knowledge systems related to foraging and food processing were lost. The dearth of documented recipes and practical guides to identifying and harvesting barnacles may have contributed to their relative obscurity.

Colombia's e-commerce market is expected to reach 13.4% of the country's retail sales in 2020, from just 2.4% in 2015. This rapid growth is driven by increasing internet penetration and the rising demand for online shopping among consumers, particularly in urban areas.
"The increasing presence of international online retailers in Colombia has also spurred local players to invest in e-commerce, resulting in a more competitive market and higher-quality services for consumers," the report said.
As a result, traditional retailers in Colombia are expected to respond to the shift in consumer behavior by adapting their operations and strategies to stay competitive.
"We see traditional retailers taking a more omni-channel approach to their businesses, blending online and offline channels to offer a seamless shopping experience for consumers," said Fernando Cano, Senior Retail Analyst at Euromonitor International.
The shift to e-commerce in Colombia is also expected to lead to a decline in the number of physical stores, as retailers reduce their brick-and-mortar presence to focus on online sales.
"However, the changing retail landscape also creates new opportunities for traditional retailers to pivot their business models and create unique experiences for consumers that can't be replicated online," said Cano.
Other findings from the report include:
The majority of online purchases in Colombia are made through mobile devices, with 73% of e-commerce sales coming from smartphones.
Online grocery shopping is becoming increasingly popular in Colombia, with 41% of online shoppers purchasing food and beverages online in 2020.
The popularity of cashless payments is on the rise in Colombia, with 44% of online consumers preferring to use credit cards or digital wallets to make online purchases.
Retailers in Colombia are investing in digital marketing and e-commerce platforms to reach consumers and increase online sales.
The shift to e-commerce in Colombia is expected to have a significant impact on the country's logistics and transportation sector, as retailers require more efficient and cost-effective delivery options to meet the rising demand for online shopping.

### Evaluation of a Distance Education Initiative
By Sandra J. Dunn. New York: Peter Lang, 1999.
This is a study of a distance education (DE) initiative in a university in Canada. The study is an attempt to evaluate the effectiveness of this initiative. Dunn, a sociologist, uses a qualitative research methodology. She argues that a non-numerical approach is more suitable for this study because DE often focuses on one-on-one communication between the instructor and student. A quantitative analysis could not capture the richness of the communication that happens in these interactions. To support her claim, Dunn conducts case studies with students and instructors participating in the DE initiative.
The book is divided into 13 chapters that deal with the introduction, methodology, and data analysis. Dunn discusses the theoretical background of DE, particularly the arguments supporting its advantages over traditional classroom settings. She explains that the research is grounded in symbolic interactionism and, as such, focuses on the social context of DE. A description of the research methodology, sampling, and data collection methods is provided in the second chapter.
The third chapter discusses the DE program that is being evaluated. Dunn highlights the features of DE that support its growth in recent years, including advances in information technology and the emergence of electronic distance education (EDE) programs. Dunn's discussion is detailed and covers both positive and negative aspects of the initiative.
A brief summary of the results is provided in chapter 4. The data were analyzed using the constant comparative method, which allowed Dunn to compare data across different categories and themes. Dunn also conducted interviews with students and instructors to gather more information on their experiences.
The case studies are presented in the following chapters. Dunn starts with three female students in a sociology of the family course who were enrolled in the DE program. The students' experiences are described through quotes and discussion of their perceptions, preferences, and the ways they maintained their identities.

EFCC raids politician’s estate, recovers N126m cash in US dollars and Naira
The Economic and Financial Crimes Commission (EFCC) has recovered over $300,000, about N126 million in Naira, in the office of a politician in Abuja, on Tuesday.
The politician’s name was not disclosed, but TheCable reports that the recovery was made at the politician’s estate in the Maitama area of Abuja.
The anti-corruption agency said the politician, who is yet to be named, was being investigated for allegations of bribery, money laundering and misappropriation of public funds.
The money recovered was said to be part of the proceeds of the politician’s alleged illicit activities.
The EFCC said the recovered money was in US dollars and Naira.
“Operatives of the Economic and Financial Crimes Commission (EFCC), yesterday, Tuesday, July 19, 2022, raided the office of a yet-to-be-named politician in Abuja, recovering $323,795.00 (Three Hundred and Twenty-Three Thousand, Seven Hundred and Ninety-Five Dollars) and N126,002,850 (One Hundred and Twenty-Six Million, Two Thousand, Eight Hundred and Fifty Naira),” a statement by Wilson Uwujaren, head of media and public affairs at the EFCC, said.
“The money, which is suspected to be proceeds of unlawful activities, was found in the politician’s office at the Maitama Estate, Abuja.
“The recovery was part of the ongoing investigation into the politician’s alleged involvement in bribery, money laundering and misappropriation of public funds.”
The EFCC said it would continue to raid the homes and offices of public officials and individuals with dubious wealth, as part of its efforts to check corruption in the country. TheCable
Since 2020, the EFCC has recovered billions of naira and dollars from politicians, public officials and individuals with dubious wealth.
For instance, in 2021, the EFCC said it recovered N9.2 billion and $97.3 million from 167 individuals and companies. The same year, the agency said it recovered over N38 billion and $13 million from politicians and individuals with dubious wealth.
The EFCC has also obtained convictions in high-profile cases, including the trial of former Governor of Delta State, James Ibori, who was jailed for 13 years for money laundering and corruption.
